current_activity: Charnwood: under the 3rd Division, supports the capture of the high ground round Point 64 north of Caen
notes: Event date: 8 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 314-315). Event definition: On the first day of Operation Charnwood General Crocker tells the 3rd Division to push armour onto the high ground (Point 64) just north of Caen and later in the morning puts his reserve, the brigade, under the division's command; in the early evening, supported by the brigade, the division captures the high ground round Point 64, overlooking Caen (pp. 314-315). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 314: "put his reserve (the 33rd Armoured Brigade) under the division's command"; p. 315: "supported by the 33rd Armoured Brigade, they captured the high ground round Point 64". Location: Lébisey, Hérouville-Saint-Clair, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Lébisey, on the ridge just north of Caen where Point 64 lies; the hill itself is not geocoded. Location support: Ellis names Point 64 just north of Caen (pp. 314-315).

current_activity: Totalize: two armoured columns with the 51st Division east of the Falaise road in the night attack
notes: Event date: 7-8 August 1944, start line crossed at 23:30 on 7 August (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 420-421). Event definition: For Operation Totalize II Canadian Corps is reinforced by the 51st Division and the brigade from I Corps; the opening attack is made by the 51st Division and the brigade east of the Falaise road, crossing a line between Soliers and St. André sur Orne at 11.30 p.m. on 7 August, in two columns each with tanks of the brigade and an infantry brigade of the 51st Division in armoured vehicles (pp. 420-421). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 420: "The opening attack would be made by the 51st Division and 33rd Armoured Brigade to the east of the Falaise road"; p. 421: "On the left of the Falaise road were two parallel columns, each with tanks of the 33rd Armoured Brigade". Location: Bourguébus, Calvados (PL0687) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Bourguébus near the start line east of the Falaise road; the columns advanced south from it during the night. Location support: Ellis puts the columns east of the Falaise road from the line Soliers-St. André (pp. 420-421).

current_activity: Astonia: with the 51st Division, attacks Le Havre from the north at midnight under artificial moonlight
notes: Event date: 10 September 1944, midnight (Ellis, vol. II, p. 14; Stacey, p. 334, gives the plan). Event definition: In the I Corps attack on Le Havre the 49th Division begins after the last bomber attack at 5.30 p.m. on the 10th; at midnight, using artificial moonlight, the 51st (Highland) Division and the brigade come in on its right attacking from the north (Ellis, p. 14); Stacey gives the plan: the 51st Division, with the brigade, would secure a base farther west on the northern edge of the Forêt de Montgeon (p. 334). Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history, and Stacey, the Canadian official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 14: "at midnight, using artificial moonlight,2 the 51st (Highland) Division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade came in on their right attacking from the north"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 334: "The 51st Division, with the 33rd Armoured Brigade, would then secure a base farther west". Location: Le Havre (PL0169) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Le Havre; the brigade attacked the northern defences of the fortress. Location support: Ellis and Stacey put the attack on the north side of Le Havre and name no village for the brigade.

current_activity: Ardennes: with the 53rd Division clears south-east of Marche and takes Grimbiémont; relieved there on 8 January
notes: Event date: 8 January 1945, the day of the relief (Ellis, vol. II, p. 190). Event definition: In the British counter-attack on the tip of the Ardennes salient the 53rd Division and the brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, clear the area south-east of Marche and capture Grimbiémont, where they are relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division (p. 190); XXX Corps had comprised the brigade from 20 December (p. 184). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 190-191: "On the left the 53rd Division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, cleared the area south-east from Marche and captured Grimbiemont, where they were relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division"; p. 184: "6th Guards and 34th Tank and the 29th and 33rd Armoured Brigades". Location: Grimbiémont, Marche-en-Famenne, Luxembourg (BE) (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the village; the day of the capture is not given, the row is the day of the relief there. Location support: Ellis names Grimbiémont (p. 190). Context: Later: Ellis, vol. II, p. 285, lists the brigade with the 31st as from the 79th Armoured Division in the Rhine crossing order of battle (23 March 1945); its independent period therefore ends between January and March 1945 on a day not given in the sources read (open question in the batch report).

current_activity: with Dutch and Belgian units prolongs the Netherlands District line to near Tiel
notes: Event date: 1945-04-13 (Stacey, p. 586).
